body:
From the pre-release security review of the server's network interface
(2026-07-26). Post-1.8.1.

## Problem

/sync was hardened against payload type confusion (T-85), but the auth routes
never were. Unauthenticated requests can crash the handler:

    POST /login    {"email": {}}  -> 500  sqlite3.ProgrammingError
                                          (Error binding parameter 0: type
                                          'dict' is not supported)
    POST /login    {"email": []}  -> 500  same
    POST /register {"email": 5}   -> 500  TypeError: expected string or
                                          bytes-like object (EMAIL_RE.match)

POST /register {"email": {}} correctly returns 422 only by accident — {} is
falsy, so validate_email's `not email` branch catches it first. A truthy
non-string (int/float) reaches the regex and raises.

Also reachable, but only with valid credentials (so post-authentication):

    POST /login {"device_label": {}} -> 500  sqlite3.ProgrammingError at the
                                             auth_tokens INSERT (auth.py:133)

No data leak: the generic Flask 500 page carries no traceback outside debug
mode, confirmed. But these are pre-auth crash paths that produce unactionable
500s in logs and monitoring, and they are inconsistent with the careful
row-scoped 422 discipline the sync engine already applies.

## Fix

- validate_email (auth.py:75): isinstance(email, str) check before the regex,
  raising the existing 422 invalid_email.
- validate_password (auth.py:80): same for password — len() on a non-string
  raises TypeError today.
- auth.login (auth.py:116): type-check email and device_label before they bind
  into SQL. device_label is also currently unvalidated for length — see the
  separate length-cap ticket.

`platform` is already handled correctly (resolve_idle_ttl_ms does an isinstance
check and falls back) — that is the pattern to follow.

## Verification

Parametrised test posting each of dict / list / int / float / None for every
top-level field of /login and /register, asserting 4xx and never 5xx.
title: auth routes: unauthenticated 500s from payload type confusion on /login and /register
